summary:
I tested the two Iroh paths that ADR-0002 §8 had only inferred, using iroh 1.3.0 (pinned).

**Rust embed.** A probe under tests/evidence/artifacts/g02-r4/x5/rust-embed/ creates two endpoints with relays, address lookup, portmapper and net-report probes off, bound only to 127.0.0.1:0. They exchange one message on ALPN heimdall/x5/0.
- All 16 builds exited 0 (4 variants × darwin-arm64 native plus x86_64/aarch64 linux-musl and x86_64 windows-gnu via cargo-zigbuild 0.23.4 and zig 0.16.0).
- ring 0.17.14 and aws-lc-sys 0.45.0 compiled under zig on every cross target. On windows-x64 both link prebuilt NASM objects shipped inside the crates.
- The darwin selftest exited 0. lsof on the exact PID showed only UDP sockets on 127.0.0.1.
- The linux-arm64 build ran in a --network none container and exited 0; /proc/net/udp had only 127.0.0.1 entries. linux-x64 also passed, but only under Rosetta emulation.
- Sizes: the frame-code baseline without iroh is about 0.30 MB. With iroh it is 3.6–6.4 MB depending on variant and target.
- Embedding iroh in a scratch copy of the frozen prototype grew it 722,144 → 4,504,064 bytes on darwin (×6.2); the other targets grew ×6.5–7.8.
- Resolved packages per target: 242–250 (iroh-default) or 232–243 (ring-min). Native-code crates: ring, blake3, and aws-lc-sys in the aws-lc variant.

**Go path.** A stdlib-only, CGO-free Go supervisor in go-helper/ starts two Rust helpers. It sends one message across the loopback iroh link through length-prefixed stdio frames, then shuts both down cleanly (all exit 0).
- It passed on darwin, in the linux-arm64 network-none container, and on linux-amd64 under emulation.
- Each helper held one 127.0.0.1 UDP socket plus one route socket. The supervisor held no inet sockets.
- When I SIGKILLed the supervisor, both helpers exited within 1.5 s.
- A Go product would ship two binaries built with two toolchains (Go 1.27.1, plus Rust 1.99.0 with zig and cargo-zigbuild for the helper). That is 8.8–11.1 MB per target, against 4.5–6.8 MB for a single Rust binary.

**Pure Go.** github.com/tmc/go-iroh v0.3.0 is a pure-Go port. It is young (first tag 2026-08-15), unaffiliated with n0 and pre-v1. It relies on a patched crypto/tls and a forked quic-go. I read its sources and did not adopt it. The other Go option, iroh-go, needs cgo and runs only on linux-musl.

**Not covered.** The Windows binaries were not run (blocked: no native Windows host).
